name.en-US: Conceptions of the Love of God

description.es-ES: Meditaciones de Santa Teresa sobre algunas palabras del Cantar de los Cantares («Béseme con ósculo de su boca…»), escritas para consuelo de sus monjas: la paz verdadera y las falsas paces, la oración de quietud y de unión, y los deseos de la esposa. Prólogo y siete capítulos, texto del P. Silverio de Santa Teresa (códice de Alba) con sus notas.
description.en-US: St. Teresa's meditations on some verses of the Song of Songs ("Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth…"), written for the consolation of her nuns: true peace and the nine kinds of false peace, the prayer of quiet and of union, and the desires of the Bride. Prologue and seven chapters; English translation by the Benedictines of Stanbrook, edited by Benedict Zimmerman, with his notes.
description.pt-BR: Meditações de Santa Teresa sobre algumas palavras do Cântico dos Cânticos, escritas para o consolo das suas monjas: a paz verdadeira e as falsas, a oração de quietude e de união, e os desejos da esposa.

sources.edition: Obras de Sta. Teresa de Jesús, ed. P. Silverio de Santa Teresa, C.D., t. IV: Moradas, Conceptos del amor de Dios, Exclamaciones (Biblioteca Mística Carmelitana), Burgos: El Monte Carmelo, 1917, pp. 211–268. Princeton Theological Seminary scan, primary OCR.
sources.description: Spanish critical text with Silverio's notes kept as footnotes; his introduction and appendices are not included. OCR of two independent scans merged word by word.
sources.tierEvidence: Teresa died in 1582; the volume was published in 1917 (public domain in the US) and P. Silverio died in 1954, so his notes are public domain under life+70 since 1 January 2025.

sources.edition: The same volume, Wellesley College scan, used as the second witness.

The Minor Works of St. Teresa, translated by the Benedictines of Stanbrook, edited with notes and an introduction by Benedict Zimmerman, O.C.D., London: Thomas Baker, 1913 (Conceptions of the Love of God, pp. 105–190). Wellesley College scan.
sources.description: English translation with Zimmerman's notes and chapter summaries; his introduction is not included. The OCR is rough: about two dozen of his footnotes are run into the text of chapters 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7.
sources.tierEvidence: Published 1913 (before 1930: public domain in the US); Zimmerman (†1937) died long ago or published anonymously over 70 years ago (UK); archive.org marks the scan NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
